title: From Hourly to Annual: How Casual Loading and Super Affect Your Pay (Plus the Mbappe Salary Comparison)
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our guide. Includes casual loading, super paid on top, and a look at the Mbappe salary for context. Fair Work figures used.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 with casual loading, giving an annual gross of $52,254.80 (excluding super).

faqs.q: How does casual loading work when converting hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When converting to annual, you multiply the loaded rate by hours per week by 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. Our [the timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). So if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer must contribute an extra $7,200 to your super fund. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy apply to my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates net pay after these deductions.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

Whether you're a full-time employee, a casual worker, or just curious about how a star footballer's earnings compare, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. Even when people search for "mbappe salary", they often see huge annual figures, but the same formula applies: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

We assume a standard 38-hour week unless you specify otherwise. This is the ordinary hours for full-time employees under the National Minimum Wage Order. For part-time or casual workers, use your actual weekly hours.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year.

If you're paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. A weekly pay of $1,140 becomes $2,280 per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the minimum for award/agreement-free adult employees. Most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement with higher rates. You can check your specific award using pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading instead of paid leave entitlements. This loading is added to the base hourly rate. So the casual National Minimum Wage is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

When converting to annual, use the loaded rate. For a casual earning $33.05 per hour for 38 hours:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80 per year.

Our [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee contributions are 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. If your annual salary is below that, super is calculated on your full earnings.

For the $30/hour example above:

Annual gross: $59,280
Super (12%): $7,113.60
Total employer cost: $66,393.60

Super does not reduce your take-home pay; it's an additional benefit. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates. For 2026–27:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (single reduction thresholds based on 2025–26 as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for an estimate after tax and Medicare.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That's about $108,352 per year. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118.40 annually.

### The Mbappe Salary in Context

When people search for "mbappe salary", they're often looking at the reported earnings of football star Kylian Mbappé, which can exceed $100 million annually. Converting that to an hourly rate (assuming a 38-hour week, 52 weeks) gives an astronomical figure – over $50,000 per hour. But for most workers, understanding your own hourly rate and how casual loading and super affect your annual pay is far more practical.

### Important Notes

- This conversion assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, explore our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) pages.
